The various diseases are difficult to discern as either empty or real; the fundamental limit and the locus of harmony lie therein. Through the power of tranquility, one may cultivate the functional application of reverence; the noble wisdom can sever the defiled dharmas of the torrential flow.

The fruit of non-returning lacks causes in the lower stages; the power and function of the cessation of the nature of entanglement and defilement subdues the fundamental inversion of contention. The visual consciousness conditions form, while the mental consciousness is the eighth; these three consciousnesses simultaneously possess the capacity for objective apprehension. This is the cause for instruction through self-nature purity; by thoroughly understanding one’s own lineage, one personally extends offerings, wherein the cultivation and veneration are vast in their temporal scope.

Seeking the power of causes to overcome defilements, hindrances, and perversions; the perfect conveyance of the cause of pure excellence; the practice of giving born of aspiration for the Mahāyāna—this is truly the ultimate realization achieved by a great man.

The power of hearing is initiated through purity; the practice is perfected in secluded places; ultimate transformation brings about harmonious benefit and relief; the nature of the superior realm is free from the marks of form; one creates inverted actions while tending toward joy; the appearance of the limit is like the nurturing love of a mother; it is fully endowed with various names and signs of generosity; and the meaning consists in the non-inverted cultivation of subduing.

The practice of equanimity is supreme and unerring; in this regard, the bodhisattva seeks the truth, and through the cultivation of compassionate vows, the teachings are accomplished. Thus, the causal characteristics of the equality of giving are preeminent.

The system is spontaneously present as the thorough knowledge of tranquility; it possesses both the application of poison and harm and the dullness and weakness [of afflictions]. The practice of generosity is supreme within the pure ultimate truth; the root of calamity is reality, and hearing and retaining [the teachings] is unerring. One thoroughly understands the subduing of all defilements and inversions; because there is no governing system, cities and towns are destroyed, and because the land is remote, the thought arises that it is difficult to go there.

The beings of the human realm are born with perverted views and dull faculties; the ten dharmas, such as pride, arise in conjunction. Their essence is truly defiled and contentious, for the nature of the view of self is a mind of contention.

The causal locus for the perfection of truth is the thorough understanding of the limit of purity and the pursuit of sublime excellence; the fetters of dust and defilement are stilled by the Noble Path. The locus of nourishment is sincerity and tranquility; from the nature of hearing, speech arises. The desires of sentient beings are defiled in their constituent parts, and therein exist inversion, darkness, conceit, and the view of self.

Purely practicing generosity with an undistorted mental state, one avoids the increasing torrent of disputes and litigation; in places of calamity and defilement where there is no giving, one remains silent and still, thereby being able to abandon bondage and染 (staining).

The mind and phenomena are truly fashioned through increase and decrease; they are pure and unerring, carrying forth that which is real. Within the realm of hungry ghosts, their actions are powerless; they are bound by their own afflictions and faults, with no release.

The supreme ultimate truth cannot be attained through any other means; one must understand the limits of desire and incline toward them. In this regard, for the sake of others, one diligently cultivates the Noble Path, thoroughly understanding the characteristics of the fetters of conduct.

Bearing the heavy burden, one seeks the extraordinary cause; giving rise to the ultimate, perfect, and final realization, one possesses the power of equanimity to understand and practice, taming with truth those who are submerged in the cycle of existence.

The various phenomena rooted in pride are defiled activities; they involve the clamor of strife and delight in craving and desire. The instructions and discourses of preceptors and others are thus of infinite pure characteristics.

One creates the causes for those karmic actions; sentient beings are conveyed so that their afflictions are stilled; inverted disputes among sentient beings are restrained; and one understands the nature of defilement through sovereign aspiration.

Truly equal, free from the bonds of craving, he practices pure giving as the most excellent among those beyond training (*aśaikṣa*); with the fundamental [wholesome roots] in accord, all afflictions (*saṃkleśa*) are exhausted; his nature possesses power, and his fetters are as virtuous as the wholesome.

In this state, the bodhisattva’s nature of the pure realm initiates discourse at the limit of all locations; through the realization that mental forms and appearances are supreme, one accomplishes the superior cause and, through faith, attains liberation.

The nature of knowledge and vision regarding the limits of arising is the characteristic of equanimity; its activity is unerring, its virtuous conduct is complete, and sentient beings therein are fearless; wherever it is established, it accords with reality.

Fundamentally unborn, it is tranquil and pure; its sovereign transformation is profound and difficult to attain. Sentient beings are originally quiescent, fully endowed with hearing and retention; it is pure, wondrous, and free from poison, realized through wisdom.

The limit of generosity consists in the appearance of rarefied desire; it is the unified branch of non-erroneous activity. Through the praise and instruction of generosity, one accords with hearing and retention, whereby the cultivation of the virtue of generosity reaches fulfillment.

The causal practices for ultimate cessation and subduing are not devoid of the dull fetters of virtuous friends; the functional power of karmic construction is rooted in the links of existence, and the occurrence of contentious disputes arises from the bonds of sovereign attachment.

Furthermore, practicing generosity without attachment amidst places of dispute, the true principle of the mental ground will manifest; by following the flow of conditioned existence and its shifting inversions, one should cultivate various practices to subdue the activities of the mind.

The Vinaya dharma is fully complete in its methods of observance and transgression; one thoroughly understands the root causes of tranquility. That which seeks generosity is pleasant and agreeable, conforming to the five types of karmic seeds of the links of existence.

From hearing the abiding place of truth, the view of self arises, leading to litigation, indulgence, and the birth of pride; yet for the great multitude of sentient beings, there is mastery in subduing them, seeking the meaning of subduing within the unborn tranquility.

Through the pure wisdom that realizes the mutual absence of substantiality, one understands the profound and true teachings of purity; this is the designation of the limit of tranquility, which directs one toward the ten paths of action of body, speech, and mind.

Pure and wondrously fashioned, it contemplates the practice of giving; it gives rise to a tranquil and equal nature; it is the causal conduct of equality in all pursuits; its fundamental basis is the fervent application of hearing; it abides immovably like a lion king; its constituent parts are complete, pure, and systematic; it is inherently sincere, supreme, and inexhaustible—the ninefold teaching of purification and discipline.

The application of the village site is inexhaustible; the practice of causes for excellent and vast food and drink results in the perfection of the awakened nature through pure, wondrous, and superior causes, just as the practice of subduing gives rise to excellence.

Having realized the nature of the elements, one transcends contention; the noble ones possess the power of impartial fruition, which is exquisite, free from strife, and delights in tranquility. Their karmic actions are sublime, serene, and free from violence.

The ten practices, such as the body of skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), involve the selfless, unerring cultivation of giving and the transformation of aspirations; they possess a fundamental excellence of sublime wisdom, are characterized by meticulous speech and excellent regulations, and manifest the supreme signs of tranquility and secrecy. They are unsurpassed within the celestial realms, most wondrous in their progression toward stillness, and free from the dust of worldly clamor, the bonds of the torrential stream, and the fundamental defilements.

In this realm, the king possesses clear insight and vision; he cherishes all living beings and dwells in profound tranquility. He subdues the frontier regions with unceasing joy, and among his precious treasures, there is none that does not embody virtuous instruction.

Having subdued both self and others, one receives the instructions of the Preceptor; all intrinsic natures and locations are equal. Through the cultivation of the sublime cause of sincerity, I am originally the sovereign creator of the established order. Free from the causes of desire, one dwells in tranquility without contention; the mind is like a master painter, creating through transformation. Hearing and seeing are ultimately dependent upon the mind; sentient beings investigate and practice the ten skillful dharmas.

The King’s practice of giving is perfect, universal, and impartial; he teaches with serene composure, never ceasing day or night. In this place, where men are dull-witted, weak, and prone to contention, disputes arise repeatedly; yet they listen to the truth. Young women suffer from afflictions and inverted desires, their thoughts continuously following the shifting transformations of sentient beings. Through various untainted and superior activities, they create manifold forms; through boundless craving, they produce dark dullness. The manifestations of affliction and the egoism that rely upon one another, together with the fundamental view of self, mutually support one another to form a hundredfold.
At what time will his virtuous conduct reach parinirvāṇa?

By practicing in accordance with the sublime path, he shall give rise to the further shore; by performing the constituent factors, he shall increase his superior power; he shall bring about the constituent factors for the world of sentient beings, and in accordance with benefit and welfare, he shall give rise to aspiration and joy.

Listening to the teachings is a beneficial cause for purity in the world; excellent indeed is the nature of generosity as a cause, which brings about the absence of hunger and thirst for those sentient beings, and through the exhaustion of inversions, one realizes the tranquility of listening.

With the perfection of practice and understanding, the defilements of inversion are exhausted; like the appearance of craving, there is no longer any pursuit. One is able to attain the vast characteristic of the absence of intrinsic nature, wherein the nature of the realms increases through reliance upon virtuous friends.

Illuminating the self-nature, one emerges from the defilement of contention; this perfected conduct accords with bliss. The links of existence are non-erroneous, the root of the world; through wisdom and tranquility, one understands bondage. Recalling the limit of the vast ultimate truth, one generates the purpose of engaging in combat. Gods and humans attain mastery, dwelling in power and stillness; the fundamental instruction is pure subduing. Understanding that generosity and wisdom are non-erroneous, one seeks the cessation of the ten types of wholesome conduct.

The king who well instructs sentient beings desiring pleasure bows his head to the noble sages who dwell in bliss and sovereignty; the secret treasury of the ten virtuous actions is the truth, which accords with the characteristics of form yet increases the locus of poison; the constituent parts possess power, fulfilling the supreme conduct.

Furthermore, during the night watches, he diligently cultivates wholesome deeds; as a man of noble character free from the conceit of self, he gives rise to the sublime and true Path, and through its perfection, he brings those multitudes under control by overturning their delusions.

With a body of equanimity and freedom from contention, possessing great power, he seeks the nature of the Triple Gem in tranquil stillness. As a man of discipline, he is able to honor those above; as a sovereign with mastery, his people all admire him. Arrogance and indulgence are stilled, the Holy Path arises, and through respectful compliance, they seek to advance toward tranquility.

In this place, the Great Being initiates excellence; dwelling in a state of sovereignty, he performs worldly deeds. Taking refuge in the ten virtues, he possesses true wisdom; for the devas, the pure, wondrous, and supreme meaning is peace and tranquility.

The gods and humans practice the penetration of both meditative concentration and non-concentrated virtue; at the edge of those torrential floods, pride is brought to rest. Through the conduct of body, speech, and mind, they cultivate the ten types of wholesome deeds. They emerge from the obstacles of affliction and are free from inverted disputes; the fundamental stillness of their activities transcends entanglements and hindrances. This is the causal practice of pure and true tranquility; those in training cultivate worldly goodness through their own nature. Regarding the characteristics of bondage and the disputes of karmic retribution, they honor and cultivate tranquility to fully understand the ripening of results.

At that time, the king practiced the ten paths of wholesome action; seeking freedom from strife and litigation, his realm was peaceful and tranquil. His regulations were strict, subduing the masses, while the veils and obscurations were as boundless as clouds covering everything everywhere. His physical appearance was radiant, reaching its ultimate excellence, and the characteristics of precious jewels were fully present within him. He gave rise to and practiced the ten types of superior cultivation, such as the giving of the body, thoroughly understanding the true, sublime, and extraordinary. Free from the defilements of pride and the like, he diminished the "self" and "dharmas," thereby severing the causes and conditions of strife, litigation, and the extremes of craving.

The nature of conditioned activity is free from contention and seeking; through the bonds of ignorance and pride, perversions arise. In this regard, the Bodhisattva understands with equanimity, hearing the truth regarding the limits of the lineage. At the time when the practice of equanimity is perfected, one realizes through tranquil cultivation and wisdom that which is to be understood. One firmly maintains the superior [wisdom] to subdue perverse conduct, thereby understanding the period of the Mahāyāna’s correct principle.

The intrinsic nature of this giving is free from malice; it subdues the beings born in the human realm through its power and function. It clearly understands the superior states of pure transformation, wherein dullness and self-conceit are fundamentally complete.

The King embodies the Great Sage and his application is boundless; having ultimately realized that the true cause is the vast cultivation of generosity, he understands the limits of temporal foundations. Through the power of the sublime cause of ultimate tranquility, the veils do not arise and afflictions are naturally extinguished.
What is the pursuit and practice of generosity?

It is when the king’s realm is secure and majestic, the people are free from litigation and capable of bearing their burdens, the hundred kinds of things arise spontaneously without decay, and the noble person remains tranquil and unmoved in whatever place they dwell.

In this state, there is no reality; one firmly cultivates the practice of parsimony. Those ten kinds of fundamental torrential floods are real; the practitioner seeking the conduct of Bodhi is a true Great Man. Through the secret wisdom, one realizes the words and deeds of the sages; darkness and pride can be abandoned through such true reality.

The source from which perverted, defiled afflictions arise is the mother, who is bound by the maiden; the benefit of subduing them lies in rigorous instruction, through which hearing becomes perfected and understanding is generated. The cause for the arising of afflictions is the predominance of the view of self (*ātman-dṛṣṭi*); one must distance oneself from each and every such perversion regarding name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*).

In this place, the king’s laws and regulations are supreme; the power of his majestic appearance is so vast that he ultimately brings forth the reality of the secret treasury, and the meaning and benefit of his speech are as profound as one could wish.

Craving can be severed by distancing oneself from its evil causes; its root is generosity, the supreme ultimate truth. Through hearing, cultivation, and practice, one seeks without error; the defilement of the view of self is stilled, and there is no fear.

The human realm accords with non-perverted disputes; the defilement of the view of self is thus stilled by silence. Bodhisattvas tame through speech; thus do those beyond training realize the principle of cessation.

Right reasoning distances one from the causes that produce conditioned activity; seeking the cessation of calamities, one exhausts the extremes of contention and defilement. Through the instruction of speech, all causes of defilement are exhausted; seeking the superior cause, one exhausts boundless defilements, and having abandoned doubt, one takes delight in the [Dharma] as a child.
What is the practice of true tranquility?

It is the elimination of the limits of pride that give rise to [defilements], the destruction of the stains of contention, and dwelling peacefully in conduct and generosity. It does not arise from expedient means that lack a cause; one seeks it and proceeds toward that place free from harm.

In this state, the three [poisons] are exhausted and the disputes of the people cease; dwelling in tranquility, all views of extremes and diminution are utterly eliminated. It gives rise to speech that is rigorous and truthful, serving as the pure and wondrous basis for the self-nature of the Noble Path. This is the fundamental locus revealed by the Great Being; endowed with the factors of existence, it cannot be harmed by poison, and through its sovereign power, it performs boundless acts of giving.

In this place, the king reveres and cultivates this supreme site; its physical appearance is majestic and beautiful, and his power is firmly established therein. Abiding peacefully at the ultimate limit, he can direct the laws and regulations; such is the unerring, serene stillness of maternal love.

One should cultivate a physical appearance of reverence and approach with solemnity; the practitioner must clearly understand the excellence of the dwelling place. The length of one's lifespan is determined by karma; this is clearly stated in the scriptures of the Vehicle, and there is no other meaning.

In this place, the Bodhisattva’s vast compassionate vows transport and deliver sentient beings to supreme fulfillment; possessing no essence of ego-conceit, there is the cause for giving, and in the state of tranquil stillness, one listens to and receives the spoken teachings.

The King of Boundless Appearance spoke thus: "Having abandoned the subtle poisons and harms of those heavens, one dwells in fundamental peace, free from contention; this gives rise to the ultimate truth, which is the reality of its cause."

The causal nature is quiescent, giving rise to powerful efficacy; through the constraints of the Dharma, one advances in practice without error. Possessing pure and wondrous causes, there is no karma of suffering; through the power of mastery, the human realm is fully perfected.

Through the inversion of craving, pride, and divergent karmic retributions, one practices giving with purity, abiding in happiness; by cultivating various superior reflections, one gains sovereign power to discipline the mental ground.

The lineage abides in the causes sought for purity; pure wisdom brings to rest the bonds of contention. In this place, the king’s laws are unerring, and his true regulations benefit and deliver the people.

The supreme practice is perfected and free from contention; having realized the ultimate truth, one is devoid of manifold pride. Having utterly extinguished the view of self upon hearing the noble speech—excellent!
Excellent! Vast is this merit.

It is the fundamental basis for the creation of the pure ultimate truth; its noble conduct is cultivated so that sentient beings may follow it. Possessing the power to transport [beings across saṃsāra], it acts as the supreme cause for practice; it seeks purity and is free from the signs of self-clinging.

Having realized the truth of the ten wholesome paths of action in silent stillness, he practiced the conduct of generosity to seek that ultimate benefit; he brought peace to the realm, subdued the borderlands, and caused the noble teachings to flourish throughout the vast royal city.

The king who skillfully bestows wisdom and understands reality, who destroys the causes of cyclic existence through the reality of pure causes, and who attains liberation through the purification of the mental consciousness—such a king is the most honored and supreme of all.

The holy power that instructs sentient beings is stern; its sentient form and appearance differ from those of the multitude. Its ultimate meaning is supreme and its aspiration is sincere; its foundation is vast, like a lion king whose physical presence is awe-inspiring.

The profound secret treasury is far removed from cyclic existence; the self-nature of the five aggregates is the perfection of the enumeration of dharmas. The dharma of the human realm allows for the cultivation of the fruit of Buddhahood; one should remain in accord with the ultimate limit of distancing oneself from strife and contention.

The power and function of fundamental quiescence can bring cessation; this is the cultivation of the Bodhisattva’s wisdom in its true nature. It is fully endowed with the ultimate mind that practices non-arising; it dwells in tranquility while transporting sentient beings, establishing boundless and supreme dharmas of meritorious action, and seeking the foundation of the system of sincerity and truth.

The definitive meaning of the Three Vehicles is as vast as a king; it is the unerring, true instruction of correct principle. Seeking through wisdom and understanding is called "unattainability. The mental factors are fundamentally quiescent, corresponding with the realization of wisdom; one understands the practice of suchness within the ground of the mind, which is unerring and pure.

The ultimate truth of all phenomena is personally realized through primordial wisdom; fundamental virtues are fully endowed with learning and retention; the mind of generosity is pure and attains non-obstruction; and through the supreme cause of non-contention, calamities and misfortunes are stilled.

The sovereign power and function give rise to mental cultivation and practice; through various causal actions, one joyfully initiates them. At the limit of pure giving, one understands and accords with it; in signless giving, there is no cognition of self or other.

Profoundly serene and tranquil, liberated and unborn, one attains the fundamental system of sovereign mastery; immovable as a mountain and possessing the strength to bear the burden, one carries sentient beings to the ultimate goal.

The causal practice of cultivation manifests as a blazing appearance; one seeks the ultimate limit and dwells in a place of detachment, reverently cultivating virtuous conduct and performing excellent acts of giving.

Thus, the nature of my view undergoes transformation; by turning away from [clinging to] non-arising, one practices true generosity. This is the arising of the fundamental cause of name-and-form, the sovereign word of praise and instruction.

In this state, the king bears the burden with equanimity; he fully understands the limits of each and every reality. The phenomena of the torrential flood do not exist as inversions, and the inversions regarding the limits of the burden are all exhausted.
The Twenty-sixth Chapter: The Meaning of the Jātaka of the Venerable Rāṣṭrapāla on the Bodhisattva’s Adornment through Giving.

Sentient beings who wander in the flow of hatred are led far away from it by hearing the Bodhisattva’s instructions. Through wisdom, they come to understand auspicious and supreme conduct; that the various natures are nothing other than karmic retribution, and that the fundamental power and function of meritorious deeds are manifold, means that those practicing with training rely entirely upon the causal ground.

The fundamental nature of the purity of name-and-form is the manifold fruition of the enjoyment of appropriate vessels; one initiates sublime conduct to perfect the cultivation of generosity, and through the power of hearing, the stainless nature is realized.

The fundamental assembly of noble ones, possessing the nature of manifold realms, seeks the pure and wondrous path of the Buddha-dharma and the holy life; through the mastery of the sphere of the function of giving, they give rise to the complete pacification of disputes and litigation.

The fundamental nature of the system is pure and vast; afflictions and disputes are unerringly stilled. The ultimate truth is established as the limit of supreme causes, remaining fundamentally unmoving and tranquil like space.

His substantial power and function are sovereign and unerring; their ultimate limit is like clouds, as the assembly of sages harmonizes. His activities are perfected and the conceit of self does not arise; through causeless practice, he receives a sublime fruition.

The non-arising of inverted defilements and pride is perfected; its fragrance is heard afar, and its karmic fruit is sovereign. It is as tranquil as space, the meaning of true liberation; it is the fundamental vehicle that accomplishes merit, and its transformations are sovereign—such is its bliss.
How does one thoroughly understand the excellent causes for superior function?

One seeks out locations, villages, and places of endeavor; in each of these, one becomes preeminent and free from obstacles like space. This ultimate truth is unerring, profound, and difficult to attain; it is in this state that the Bodhisattva practices giving for a long duration.

The nature of the ten wholesome paths accords with cessation; the fundamental nature of afflictions does not arise. Attachment to the view of self gives rise to the obscuration of defilement; as the retribution conforms to its form, there is no means by which it may be abandoned.

In this place, there is further the mental cultivation and practice, the instruction on the characteristics of tranquility and perfect purity, the vastness of power and function, and the upright majesty of appearance; the resulting karmic rewards are supreme and never diminish.

The fragrance of superior wholesome karma is heard afar; impartial giving gives rise to fulfillment; pure, wondrous, and sublime cultivation honors the ultimate truth; and past conformity arises from causes free of pride.

Hearing the sublime brings about the distancing of ignorance; the ultimate truth is thoroughly purified in both self and other. Cultivating the fundamental characteristics of non-self through generosity, one does not give rise to the meditative absorption that creates enmity.

Equally adorned and free from defilement and contention, it is fully endowed with the non-arising of disputes; the fundamental causes of strife are stilled and brought to rest. Such is the harmony and tranquility of the virtue of precepts:

because of anger there is contention, yet one remains solemnly distant from it; when the pure mind is aroused, the duration of its time is extended; the ultimate limit of its true nature is self-evident, and the characteristics of its cultivation manifest as its own physical retribution. Because of shifting signs, sudden violence may arise, yet through clarity and transparency, the retribution becomes perfected.

Cultivation through superior effort becomes pure, exquisite, and lovely; it is without diminution, being tranquil, pure, and radiant. Its function is to bestow mastery upon all that is sought, and one understands that the true cause of the characteristics of form is wisdom.

In this place, there is the karmic fruition of kingship that accords with one's wishes; the location is sovereign, pure, and immaculate; distant things are known as clearly as if seen with one's own eyes; and the systems sought after are unerring and true.

Tending toward the activity associated with the marks of form, one should respond so as to fulfill the past and manifest the present; by moving toward that, the greed and delusion of self and other naturally subside, and at this point, the understanding of wisdom is attained of itself without being far off.

Having realized existence and non-existence, the mind gives rise to non-erroneousness; the bonds of craving cease, and one cultivates mastery in giving. Afflictions diminish like food and drink in a flowing stream; carrying oneself and others is like the regulations of a king.

Perceiving, hearing, and understanding the reality of each and every thing, one awakens to and comprehends them within the state of profound stillness; through the power and function arising from the limits of language, though things may be far apart, they are as if face-to-face.

Furthermore, through long-term, perfect, and compliant practice, one’s physical form becomes sublime and exhausts all perversions; one understands the cultivation of meditative abiding and cessation, and awakens to the radiant splendor of the shore of enlightenment—the secret stillness.

One gives rise to non-erroneous elimination of attachment; defilements, decay, and decline are purified without replacement. The nature of defilement is exhausted in truthful cessation, and one realizes the vast and powerful function of reality. Seeking the fulfillment of those aggregate characteristics in accordance with them, one initiates tranquility amidst the shifting transformations of the torrential flow. The secret treasury is profoundly deep and originally without form; it is the fundamental basis for abiding in stillness in accordance with its own nature.

The inverted practices constitute defilement and calamity; the burden of afflictions gives rise to functional power. Through the mutual causality of the constituent parts, one advances without bondage, following and comprehending the supreme practices that are difficult to perform.

There is nothing to be sought or pursued; the characteristics of inverted birth arise like clouds at the limit of existence. The self-nature of afflictions is pure and wondrous, and through the net of giving, all calamities are brought to rest. The nature of the realm of the ten difficult-to-practice virtues is truly real.

The characteristics of pride in the world are sovereignity, the root of perverted attachment and bondage, the superior transformation of karmic fruition, and the cultivation of practice; one fully understands that the fragrance of ethical discipline is richly aromatic.

Such a king’s appearance is worthy of admiration; his karmic fruition is supreme and peerless in the world. Possessing the nature of equanimity, he practices the ten paths of wholesome action; his merit is exalted, perfect, and beyond compare.

In this realm, the sovereign’s institutions are universally equitable; for the benefit and welfare of living beings, sacred power is paramount. Through wisdom and understanding, he knows how the people flock to him, and all his edicts are tranquil and impartial.

This is an auspicious omen within the realm of this Great Man: that there is a king therein who is fully endowed with hearing and retention; whose legal proceedings are free from inversion; whose holy power is immovable; in whose land no reports of famine or scarcity are heard; who practices the difficult task of giving without error toward the Triple Gem; and who possesses pure, wondrous power to hear the truth with sincerity.

In this state, the Bodhisattva fundamentally practices generosity, giving rise to power and function that are quiescent and perfect; when it arises in the mental ground, there is no bondage, and the supreme ultimate meaning is world-transcendent silence.

Equanimity transforms and creates without contention; the power and function of arising reach the limit of tranquility. Ignorance and strife suddenly cease; a compassionate mother’s love for transformation is unending. Hunger and thirst are stilled, thereby bringing peace and happiness; vast vows of compassion seek the goal inexhaustibly.

I see that the mind does not arise; it tends toward reality, the sovereign limit, and the peerless intrinsic nature. The dwelling place of sentient beings is supreme and free from contention; that fundamental wisdom is realized as being ungraspable.

The power and function of name-and-form are as quiescent as space; it is the secret fundamental state of harmonious integration. In this place, the nature of the aggregates is accumulated through conditioned activity; its inverted defilements and limits are peerless.

Sentient beings take diligence as their fundamental nature; thus arises the manifestation of non-self. Bearing the burden to its ultimate limit through a single unifying function, they dwell in a state of tranquil non-contention, like a house that is empty space.

It is difficult to establish the root of signlessness; one seeks non-contention and unerring practice, dwelling in tranquility through the distinguished factors of causal signs, wherein selflessness brings about cessation.

In that realm of transition and change, the seeker of the path of learning exerts their intent to practice so that calamities and afflictions are completely stilled; through the arising of the superior state, cultivation and reverence remain indestructible. The boundaries of space and the characteristics of form can be fashioned, while the system is vast and its nature fundamentally quiescent; the perfected manifestation is pure, wondrous, and worthy of reliance.

The secret nature of non-arrogance possesses its own power; furthermore, there is the nature of the accumulated aggregates at their limit. Fully endowed with the conceit of "I," it establishes the nature of an ordinary being, yet swiftly proceeds toward the non-contentious state where wholesome seeds arise.

These great beings establish their minds in abiding; they cultivate giving with tranquility like space and equanimity; they dwell in stillness, free from signs and far removed from alarm and fear; they are silent and still like space, originally signless.

The nature of conceptualization is most supreme; such instruction is entirely non-erroneous. In this regard, seeking precious objects and practicing generosity constitutes the non-perverted characteristic of the noble path of giving.

True giving is tranquil and effortless, carrying the three vehicles across to the other shore; it is quiescent and non-arising, sovereign and true. Its physical manifestations are serene, and its cultivation of power is profound. Day and night, throughout the six periods, it carries beings forward without ceasing; though associated with afflictions, the mind cultivated therein is brought to rest.

The King, with his noble wisdom, observes all within his realm; he never abandons any being born into his lineage. "One should cultivate weary detachment," such are the words of the Buddha. Through generosity free from pride, one attains the pure, wondrous, ultimate, and impartial wisdom of a Buddha.
What is meant by "the seeds of rebirth have not yet been severed"?

It refers to a situation where there is a king who benefits and relieves the poor and destitute, yet remains bound by craving and attachment, practicing defiled conduct; his physical existence is not yet exhausted, and his inverted views have not been stilled.

Thus, as the locus of conditioned activity shifts, one fulfills the hearing of the Dharma and practices the path of correct principle; with sublime physical marks and the cessation of enmity, there is no sense of self-conceit.

The cause for inducing those reflections is the power of a spiritual friend and a vast mind; it gives rise to the natural state of the bestowed instructions on cessation, wherein one accords with the ultimate truth and is far removed from the view of self.

In this realm and land, one cultivates pure conduct; through the power of mastery, one practices generosity like a celestial being. Disputes do not arise, for the power of the sages can bring them to rest; as activity unfolds, pride is brought to cessation.

A virtuous mind is difficult to generate, yet it can be attained through diligent pursuit; abiding in tranquility and corresponding with it, one remains far removed from greed, hatred, and delusion; the fundamental ultimate truth is free from the bonds of contention; and through perfect hearing, one attains impartial sovereignty.

The secret of the non-arising of such a view of self is like a king who is supreme among men; his physical marks are perfected through the practices of previous lives, as spoken by the original sages regarding the mastery of sentient beings.

The length of one’s lifespan resulting from karmic actions is brought about by the cultivation of noble practices; it is through the most supreme generosity and single-minded cultivation that one attains this.

Sentient beings seek out and abandon the poisons of enmity, and by listening with power, they cultivate the practice of giving. The manifestation of physical form is produced through the power of vows; yet, the appearance of causelessness is a fabrication of delusion and darkness, such that these various classes of beings find it difficult to escape their fetters.

In this state, the bodhisattva truly possesses wisdom; bearing the burden of sentient beings to liberate them from the hardships of hunger and thirst, they aspire to generosity and accord with the virtue of the precepts. Being forever free from contention, they possess wise understanding; they cultivate the practice of giving exhaustively so that afflictions do not arise, acting according to the wisdom of causes.

Sentient beings who are dull-witted are bound by the cords of their own negligence; their afflictions are thus never far removed, just as a great king bears the burden of the borderlands, administering laws with impartiality without ever ceasing.

When living beings give rise to arrogance, strict regulations must be established; when compassion and wisdom arise together, there is corresponding understanding. The commands of these three will surely issue forth at the proper time, so that through rigorous systems, such matters shall not recur.

The cessation of seeking after gain and profit is called the state where name-and-form are without fear and self-clinging is abandoned; at this time, the characteristics of the stage possess their own benefit, and peaceful, composed action constitutes the instruction for Bodhisattvas.

Thus, when a king’s desire and greed are vast, he bears the burden of the frontiers and the four distant regions who follow and submit to him; though there is no cause for boundless, extraordinary suffering or pain, his view of self is stained and exhausted, yet affliction does not arise. Such inverted attachment is no less than hunger and thirst, and the bonds of craving rooted in pride truly exist.

Understanding the systems of power in the borderlands, one dwells in tranquility with a mind free from pride; through the self-nature of the body and a purified mind, there is no ground for the arising of the torrential afflictions.

The mind lacks reverence and arrogance increases; there is no end to the lack of awe and fear regarding the observance of precepts. Having realized that one's own nature is fundamentally true and real, one continues practicing generosity for a long duration without ceasing.

The seeker cultivates the nature of non-erroneous practice, giving rise to the intention to cultivate and nurturing the sprouts of goodness; it is the foundation of the path of tranquil and fearless conduct, wherein one personally practices generosity while fundamentally remaining free from signs.

Seeking the truth within the characteristics of the pure and wondrous aggregates, with the nature of cow’s milk as a metaphor for its ultimate limit; taking the equality of the supreme meaning and tranquility as the foundation, one remains far removed from the defilement of contention and dwells in peaceful cessation. In this dwelling of fearlessness, looking in all directions without concealment, the practice of pure serenity is unerring and true; when the view of self is relinquished, disputes and litigation cease of their own accord.
How is it that one becomes tranquil and detached from the self and what belongs to the self?

In this regard, there is a king who practices pure and sublime generosity; he provides protection from fear in the borderlands and bestows impartial aid. Through his governance, living beings attain peace, and they seek the time-honored foundations of the Noble Teachings.

Perfectly fulfilling the view of self and remaining far removed from it, the mental ground is ultimately purified like space; thus, the equality of mind and phenomena arises, and one attains the fearless cultivation of noble conduct.

The Bodhisattva’s instruction is to cherish and nurture the body; to exhaust the limits of inversion and abide in the perfection of the self-view while remaining far removed from it; and to reach the ultimate limit of the ultimate truth, which is characterized by indestructibility.

Possessing the faculty of hearing and retaining, they have stilled arrogance; they realize the noble cause of the fundamental nature of phenomena, which is the root of liberation. Through the practice of giving, they cease anger and ceaseless contention, and are able to destroy craving, transforming it into purity.

In the training precepts there is no fear, for one thoroughly understands non-self; one departs from the defilement of contention and engages in what is real. Through the excellence of moderation in food and drink, sublime speech reaches a state of solemnity.

Such is the ultimate nature of transformation; it can be attained through the instructions and constraints of a compassionate mother. Free from those errors of inversion, suffering, and afflictions, the cessation of defilements brings about supreme happiness.
Seeking the purification and cessation of disputes, such is the supreme sovereignty of merit.

Past actions that have arisen are free from contention; there, the extremes of ignorance and pride are stilled through *dhyāna*. One fashions worthy vessels to make offerings to the Triple Gem, cultivating the causes for the transformative power of noble wisdom.
The Garland of the Buddha’s Former Births (Bodhisattvāvadānamālā), Fascicle Twelve.
The Garland of the Buddha’s Former Births, Fascicle Thirteen.
Composed by the Noble Vīrasena and others.

Translated by Imperial Decree by the Great Master of Sanskrit Scholarship Shao De Hui Xun and others, including the Song Dynasty Court Rank of San Dafu and Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, for the purpose of translating the scriptures: This truly virtuous and pure conduct exhausts the marks of defilement and bondage, thereby attaining peace and happiness; such supreme meaning is entirely equal, giving rise to the perfection of generosity and tranquil stillness.

The cultivation of the causes for the ultimate truth is preeminent and powerful; the power to pacify afflictions is sovereign; the performance of secret practices is sovereign and truthful; and the blazing cultivation of the causes of name-and-form is indestructible.

In those who practice the ten wholesome actions, afflictions do not arise; they are able to maintain the power of their own intrinsically pure nature, and the phenomena of time and circumstance accord with tranquility. Thus, when a king cultivates and honors the Way and its Virtue, it is inexhaustible.

Through the power of application, one practices the perfection of giving; through ultimate purity, one listens to the teachings and ceases evil. All forms of happiness can transport one there; pure speech is inherently the sovereign.

Thus, these noble dharmas are meaningful, beneficial, and tranquil; they achieve perfect instruction, are powerful, unerring, and pure. Superior sentient beings do not give rise to self-grasping; the King is able to skillfully teach such unerring accordance with cessation, whereby those in the stage of training possess the power to seek out and be conveyed [to liberation].
How does one obtain the cause of the sublime and excellent?

By practicing without fear, one reaches the ultimate goal of the three vehicles. When those gods, free from anger, gather in truth, they possess the power to accord with the limits of obstructive defilements; thus do the fetters of the world arise.

The fundamental basis for sentient beings in the desire realm heavens exists as name-and-form, which is pure, subtle, beneficial, and true; these sublime beings act according to their fundamental nature, and their ultimate reality consists of boundless merit.

The fundamental holy power of the Tathāgata is perfected; he truly manifests the cessation of unwholesome dharmas. The compassionate vow fulfills the royal decree, and such worthy vessels are reverently honored by devas and humans. Wisdom is exercised as the system of holy power.
How does that wisdom arise and seek its goal?
Thus, through reverent cultivation, one realizes the truth of wisdom and understanding.
This is the twenty-seventh chapter on the meaning of the Jātaka of the Venerable Rāṣṭrapāla, concerning the Bodhisattva’s practice adorned with generosity.
Pure, true, exhaustive, and free from defilement or contention, it is the perfect manifestation of the vast limit of bitter suffering—the so-called hearing of the Bodhisattva’s instructions.
How does one seek and pursue conduct free from affliction?

Inversion, ignorance, pride, desire, and greed are meaningless; they represent the ultimate limit of the quiescence of sentient beings. Greed, hatred, and delusion are fundamentally meaningless at their root; with these unwholesome roots such as pride and other afflictions as conditions, one gives rise to all manner of suffering and distress.

The ultimate fundamental limit of fearlessness is the true nature of the causes and conditions of craving and pride; the activities of sentient beings cease and do not arise, and through the stainless practice of pure dharmas, the arising of poisonous harm and inverted cognition is prevented.

The causes of hunger and thirst are the retribution of afflictions; following after perversion, one’s observance of precepts is deficient, the hearing of meaningful benefit ceases and does not arise, and afflictions such as pride continue to arise in succession.

Generosity, loving-kindness, and patience are ultimately perfected without cause; their phenomenal forms are fundamentally empty and cannot be attained through cultivation; only when the torrential floods are forever severed is the practice of patience truly accomplished.

One realizes the destruction of the world through awakened awareness; with mastery over advancing and withdrawing, one’s wisdom and understanding become clear and lucid. One accomplishes the signs of a state that is tranquil and detached; the self-nature is quiescent, pure, and stilled.

I reverently honor the supreme one who possesses sublime realization, whose conduct of patience and compassion reaches the limit of liberation; whose nature of name-and-form is subject to disintegration, yet who completes the perfections through the power of lifelong practice, prioritizing patience and ethical discipline.

The seed-consciousness is the true, ultimate, and unerring reality; the darkness, dullness, and obscurations are all exhausted without limit, and in that state of practicing generosity, speech is stilled.
How does one distance oneself from the profound dharmas of the stage of training?

In this state, one cultivates the vast non-self and practices all manner of universal non-duality; the reward of nurturing such supreme characteristics is like a lotus that opens and closes, its fragrance wafting afar, stainless and pure, with no dust arising.

The realm of the nation is situated in the center, free from sudden violence; it eliminates the signs of arrogance and reaches the limit of right practice. The vessels [of sentient beings] are equal, without distinction between self and other; the characteristics of the limbs and the mental ground undergo transformation.

Free from the pursuit of worldly gain and devoid of the nature of pride, one gives rise to mastery; among the gods and those still in training, there is purity and excellence, yet no arrogance and no arising of afflictions. One thoroughly understands the exhaustion of signs, and through superior hearing, one’s speech is sincere; regarding fundamental calamities, one possesses the capacity to bear them.
What is the thorough understanding of the true characteristics of the body, in accordance with the fulfillment of transformative cultivation?

In this regard, when a king gives rise to the mind of generosity, he possesses the qualities of hearing and retention and cultivates marks of reverence; amidst disputes, litigation, and hardships, his movements remain impartial, and his superior wisdom gives rise to instruction.

Seeking the truth in a state of tranquility, one is able to establish systems and regulations within the various directions; through the ultimate limit of giving, the reality of form and mind is perfected, and through reverent service, the excellence of virtuous generosity is fully realized.

Through the power and function of signlessness, one constructs and brings forth a land fully endowed with sublime characteristics; by seeking the supreme goal, training in study, hearing, and retention, one cultivates vast causes, whereby that stainless limit of hearing and retention becomes preeminent.

The nature of the Tathāgata is inherently tranquil and silent; its adornments are equal and free from inverted characteristics. Name-and-form are most supreme, pure, subtle, and fragrant; through the cultivation and exaltation of the ten wholesome paths, afflictions are transformed.

At the stage of the mental ground, there is tranquility in each respective state; the roots of the torrential afflictions are utterly removed; one delights in adornment and remains serene in every movement; and the three fundamental wisdoms are cool and sublime.

Exercising the power of generosity through sovereign physical forms, one possesses the full capacity for hearing and retaining the teachings without pride; by shifting and generating the fundamental characteristics, one distances oneself from craving and pursues the supreme state.

The correct practice of the ten wholesome paths involves the cessation of defilements; it nurtures non-contention and brings the exhaustion and stilling of fear. When the view of self arises again, it gives rise to afflictions; therefore, one must cultivate the superior practice that engenders purity.

Merit and tranquility give rise to reality; the torrential flow of inversion is the fundamental truth. The manifestation of appearances gives rise to pure systems; thus, the nature of such types of pride is destroyed.

Virtuous conduct is cultivated with sublime purity and detachment; through the true system, name-and-form arise. In the state of tranquility, there is desire, craving, hunger, and thirst; wherever one follows, the constituent parts are perfected.

The complete array of pits and traps for nurturing and transforming beings brings auspiciousness; through wisdom one understands the source of the arising of pride, which is the fundamental power and function of vast tranquility; this is the state of the cool, pure, and wondrous limit.

Fully understanding the realms of existence, the conceit of "I" does not arise; through the supremacy of tranquility, all defilements are exhausted. One carries out the true teaching of the ten wholesome paths.

Just as the karma created by those in the realm of hungry ghosts is incomparable, one bears the burden of roots of goodness through hearing and retention, establishing them through what has been heard. Abiding in equanimity regarding these appearances, there is no place for inverted defilements to rely upon.

Thoroughly understanding the distancing from the defilements of dullness and obstruction, one relies with mastery upon the pursuit of cultivation; this accords with the fundamental nature of true transformation and is the unerring, pure foundation of form and characteristics.

The vast arising of compassionate nurture constitutes the foundation for delighting in hearing and upholding [the Dharma] and for being carried across; the performance of desire is the nature of perversion, and the creation of strife and litigation yields no superior fruit.

The binding of signs and characteristics does not exist as a dominant factor; ultimately, all shifting appearances are exhausted. There is attachment to the nurturing of that which involves contention and defilement; the defilement of the afflictive hindrances increases through inversion.

In this realm, sentient beings engage in the clamor of the view of self and perform the karmic causes of inversion, pride, and so forth; yet the King practices virtuous instruction with perfect hearing and retention, remaining unshakable in the practice of patience, attaining the supreme tranquility and cessation obtained through the distancing of various fevers of affliction and the bonds of defilement.

Wisdom penetrates the three natures and is associated with the mental faculty; it is the dominant cultivation that functions as a torrential stream of defiled wisdom. Its power and function possess substantiality and autonomous transformation, yet within the aggregate of formations (*saṃskāra-skandha*), there is no arising, and thus no basis for transformation.

The cessation of evil is the ultimate truth; hearing is equal. Thus, one increases the cultivation of detachment from the torrent [of afflictions]. Hearing establishes the limit of "self" and "mine," whereby the defilements and bonds of the mental ground (*manobhūmi*) are truly stilled and removed.

Ultimately, one realizes the cessation of the ten wholesome paths; pure generosity blazes with increasing intensity; the fundamental power and function is the stillness of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*); through correspondence with generosity, all piercing pains and poisons are exhausted; the fundamental burdening of obscurations and defilements is completely stilled; the power and function of the teaching’s Dharma are secret and unerring; and the limits of the ten wholesome paths cause all derivative categories to cease.

In this place, there is a queen who presides as sovereign; she practices the ten virtuous deeds in accordance with ultimate reality. The sentient beings of the celestial realms possess superior physical forms, and the fundamental truth of the pure Vinaya gives rise to the pure activities of intentional meaning.

In the celestial realms, one truly delights in cultivating generosity; by taming sentient beings, wisdom is further generated. Through mental awareness, one gives rise to purposeful action, and the power of the mind-body becomes perfectly sublime. One initiates pure giving, and women remain far removed from such practice.

Having thoroughly understood the meaning and benefit of the supreme cause of happiness, one possesses the power of the ultimate limit of superior knowledge and vision; remaining unimpaired, one unfailingly accords with the secret, which is the fundamental root of the factors of the mental ground’s intrinsic nature.

Invoke the reality of one’s fundamental practice; remain far removed from negligence and cultivate pure generosity; align the path of practice with auspicious signs, names, and forms; and seek instruction for the sake of supreme benefit.

Perversion and defilement make happiness difficult to cultivate; dwelling in tranquility amidst change allows for the realization of coolness. Through the arising of wholesome giving, one develops non-perverted mindfulness; thus, the practice of generosity and ethical conduct increases superior merit and virtue.

The ultimate excellence is the supreme culmination; it is the noble vehicle that carries one toward harmonious purity. It is the state of perfect, pure liberation, characterized by the supreme aspect; its essential nature is non-illusory, supremely powerful, and abides in the reality of truth.

Such non-erroneous cultivation to the ultimate limit possesses the power to pierce through the various practices of the path; it is the practice of signlessness within the nature of equality, the causal conduct of true reality that is quiescent by its very nature.

Virtuous deeds can be applied through harmony and detachment; there is the noble foundation of selflessness and progress; there is the cultivation of causes for those in training, characterized by supreme secrecy; and amidst the torrential afflictions, one remains supremely immovable.

The essence of form is fundamentally mind, and mind is likewise fundamentally born; to understand that seeking is like the characteristic of space, the activities of ultimate reality are stilled, and since the root does not arise, how could there be any longing?

The meaning of right liberation is non-reliance; its cause of arising is quiescent, pure, and without cultivation. Through hearing, practicing generosity, and remaining silent and still, one seeks peace; thus, when afflictions arise in the mind, they are initiated as purity.

The power and function of this fundamental practice of giving are supreme and indestructible; they carry one across without error. One thoroughly understands that its characteristics are fundamentally non-arising and thus not ablaze. Being thus without error and possessing power, the extremes of pride can be stilled through true purity and excellence.

Through meditative concentration, the mind becomes tranquil and still; by hearing the teachings, worldly fears can be exhausted. Such excellence in the practice of patience is the ultimate cause for uprooting the afflictions.

The intrinsic nature possesses the power to fully understand and transport; through hearing its characteristics, one delights in and nurtures it. The ultimate intrinsic nature is the transformation of merit; far removed from various locations and boundaries, one seeks meritorious karma and attains the cessation of the ultimate truth. Through non-erroneous conduct, one cultivates the causes for bearing this burden.

In the state of the pure intrinsic nature, which is tranquil, one accomplishes the flow of meritorious deeds and remains far removed from cyclic existence; the boundaries of the torrential floods are brought to rest, and through the harmonious perfection of pure cultivation, one attains fulfillment.

The functioning of perverted afflictions is real; where wisdom resides in giving, it possesses power. When sentient beings' afflictions are purified, wisdom does not arise [as a separate entity]; the capacity to bear the burden of virtue is the fundamental source of power and function.

One cultivates the practice of the world's meaningful benefits; the creation of limits possesses powerful equanimity; the forceful activity of violent sentient beings is inverted; and the fundamental nature is the sublime appearance of generosity.

Cultivate loving-kindness and the practice of patience for the sake of tranquility and benefit; repent to achieve purity and gain understanding of the teachings; maintain the secret through wisdom and restraint; and cherish and honor the nature of equality.

Adorned with power and the pure, wondrous nature, through the supreme teachings at the limit of causal practice, one abandons hunger and thirst for liberation and tranquility; that which is truly fashioned is thus entirely exhausted, and the causes of defilement dwelling in pride are brought to cessation.

This is the teaching on the purity of the cause of equality; herein, a king practices the perfection of giving, seeking the fruit of Buddhahood with pure, wondrous, and unerring resolve, while a son of good family cultivates generosity accordingly.

In the celestial realms, such is the peaceful conveyance for practicing the path to the further shore; at the limit of time, there is the excellence of delight. Such is the sublime limit of these gods, wherein they give rise to a true state of peace free from pride.

The ultimate mode of being is quiescent and serene; its pure power and function are like a celestial king. Having understood the fundamental locus of the true limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), one establishes the fundamental characteristics of purity.

One thoroughly understands the afflictions of the ten types [of beings], the power and function of the truthful reality of their abodes, the fundamental nature of the realms which are like a covering veil, and the limits of calamities and misfortunes within those abodes as if in pits and traps. One practices generosity with mastery, remains far removed from strife and litigation, and increases toward the truthful reality through superior purity and excellence.

One thoroughly understands the progression of transformations according to their respective powers and functions; with a body of mind free from defilement, pure and selfless, one acts as the fundamental basis for the power and function of sublime characteristics. Far removed from extreme tendencies toward greed, one brings them to rest; following virtuous friends, one practices tranquility and generosity, purifying the nature of ignorance and pride through instruction.

The King completely brings to rest the fundamental fetters and thoroughly understands the nature of past entanglements that arise from inversion; he accords with the cessation of the designations of afflictions.
Sentient beings who harbor such conceptualizations are dull and obscured.

True transformation gives rise to tranquility; inverted defilements are as boundless as space. Fabricated transformations and the darkness of pride persist; afflictions and inversions ultimately constitute defiled obstructions, while pure instruction is serene and non-existent.

The activities of those various inversions are real; craving and attachment constitute their fundamental substance. These are the predominant defiled inversions and the torrential flow of defiled phenomena, which possess the power to produce the characteristics of defiled obstructions.

The view of self is the root, which is difficult for non-sages to sever; it is severed by the fundamental wisdom (*mūla-jñāna*) upon the path of seeing (*darśana-mārga*) of the three vehicles. Thereupon, all remaining afflictions are extinguished and ultimately do not arise; this is the limit of remoteness. It is the reality of truth, like space, non-erroneous, and quiescent. For those first learning on the mental ground, the mind is set at ease and sovereign, and the marks of the body are perfected.

Those who are bound by the nature of the envelopments and hindrances, who are dull-witted, fettered, and whose conduct is defiled, even though the gods may exercise sovereignty and practice such veneration, their essence remains bound by defilement, having afflictions as its nature; thus, the view of self arises as the root of defiled wisdom.

The causes for the arising of purity cease within sentient beings; the power and function of the King’s commands do not waver; dullness, arrogance, and egoism are purified and abandoned—thus is the limit of the world well-cultivated.
What is the reality of the lifespan’s intrinsic nature, its abiding, its vessel-like function, and its utility?

That which is the true meaning of giving possesses a non-erroneous nature; it is the pure cessation of the limits of pride, and its causal nature is the virtuous and pure creation of formative activity.
What is the cultivation of the excellence of giving?

Fundamental ego-clinging gives rise to arrogance and indulgence; by ceasing these shifting transformations, one attains the distinction of ultimate truth. To fully comprehend this and seek the realization of reality is the profound purport of the King’s adornment of the mental ground.

The fundamental limit is the ultimate self-nature; the purity of mind is the excellence of true generosity; the manifestation of the pure self-nature is the practice of cultivation; the power generated at the site of arising is the practice of cultivation; and being endowed with hearing and retention, one destroys the world.
What is the cessation of the purification of the branches?
It is the secret fundamental of existence and non-existence; when a king understands the regulations for living beings, pure precepts are accumulated and brought forth therein.

Mutually manifesting true anger, pride, and the signs of bondage and contention, gods and humans exert power to cultivate practice; through superior detachment, they understand the nature of karmic activity and bring calamities to a halt through their excellence. Fully possessing fundamental bonds, defilements, inversions, and dullness, they impartially comprehend these bonds, defilements, and contentions.

The cause for excellence in the pure and wondrous realms of the gods is the instruction of the noble ones regarding the limits of patient practice; the nature of the entanglements of the afflictive obscurations is such that the King issues his commands, which the noble wisdom fully understands; thus, through the supreme culmination of exalted practice, one realizes the fundamental category of inverted views and overweening pride.

The nature of the Tathāgata is truly without self; the root of calamity is quiescent and utterly exhausted; its profound, unerring power and function are sovereign, and the essential nature of the torrent of afflictions can be brought to an end.

One thoroughly understands that women give rise to profound faults and afflictions; one realizes that their physical forms and appearances are ultimately inverted and that the components of their ego-clinging are likewise inverted and non-existent; thus, by relying on the teachings of the Noble Ones, one gains the power of generosity.

Sentient beings are without poison; that is the ultimate truth (*paramārthasatya*). Furthermore, it is the supreme cause, the fundamental self-nature (*svabhāva*), wherein the stains of the limb of craving are exhausted and name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*) do not exist. It is the tranquil and secret mark of gods and humans, where dullness, pride, and the defilements of malevolent spirits are stilled. Those bonds are eternally severed at the limit of the body, and the ten types of fundamental defilements are stilled by the noble ones (*ārya*).

In this place, the defilements of devas and humans are destroyed; hatred ceases and karmic formations do not arise. Through supreme causes, fearlessness, and the realization of tranquility, the sovereign bears the burden of distant realms until they are stilled. The marks of mastery are truly devoid of activity, for the nature of purity is far removed from malevolent spirits.

Knowing that women are the root of obstacles to the good, this is the true time for devas and humans; free from the practice of anger, they cultivate tranquility, and as the causes of purity manifest, disputes have already ceased.

The king bears the burden of living beings; when the correct principle prevails, the five aggregates are truly established. Through superior cultivation, defilements are distanced, and mastery is exercised through fundamental application.

The cause of mastery over physical form is the reality of practice; when conceptualization has ceased, there is the mutual power and function. Fear is exhausted in the supreme ultimate truth, wherein calamities and misfortunes are truly stilled. Without the marks of destruction or the defilement of transformation, the sovereign’s enacted systems of governance are brought to rest.

Thus, while the calamities of water, fire, and wind may occur within the higher and lower realms of the celestial migrations (*deva-gati*), these three calamities cease entirely in the fourth dhyāna heaven. Therein, the arising of pure goodness brings about the realization of the torrential flow [of afflictions]. Among the dharmas of hatred present throughout the three realms, there are two types corresponding to the seven secondary afflictions such as anger (*krodha*). Within the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), there are the two dharmas of guile (*śāṭhya*) and deceit (*māyā*); in the two lower stages [of the form realm], there are the nine root [afflictions]; and among the minor secondary afflictions, there is pride (*mada*), while among the major secondary afflictions, there are eight. These are all understood to extend to the limits of the three realms.

Reverently cultivating the constituent parts of pure action, one seeks to bring an end to calamities through the power of the root; herein the Bodhisattva perfects the power of patience, and through the true efficacy of pure giving, they correspondingly transport others with the fullness of hearing and retention. Seeking to eliminate darkness and pride through the fundamental characteristics of form, one briefly explains the perfection of the practice of the precepts, wherein the power of the pure, supreme cause brings an end to defilement.

With superior compassion, vows, and ego-inflation all exhausted, one accords with and pursues the Tathāgata’s discourse; possessing the pure merit of unerring self-nature, one thoroughly understands the limits of association with afflictions; reflecting upon the categories of good and evil destinies as well as spiritual friends, one thus gives rise to the supreme mind amidst suffering and distress, and excels in hearing and retaining the teachings.

The transformations and bondages that afflict sentient beings arise from arrogance and indulgence in desire; through the cause of superior tranquility, they cease of their own accord. As various afflictions are stilled by the wholesome mind, the nature of defiled evil is distanced and no longer arises.

Name-and-form is the potent, wondrous cause of the five aggregates; its root is quiescent, non-erroneous, and pure. Its indestructible power is the pure intrinsic nature, which seeks the exhaustion of calamities through the cessation of instruction.

With the physical body as the basis, sentient beings proceed according to their past karma; when those signs are exhausted, the learner’s excellence increases, the fundamental nature of the body is quiescent, and one cultivates the practice of non-self through the teachings of the ultimate truth.

The great Dharma of purity is preeminent in its benefit; one realizes truth and remains far removed from the bonds of defilement. Through various modes of transport, one practices generosity at the proper time; its sublime appearance is the reality of tranquility.

The karma of the fruit of Arhatship having been exhausted, one attains superior physical marks in those respective abodes; through hearing, retention, and making offerings, one seeks the state of tranquility. One perfectly honors that mark of ultimate reality, reaching the limit of benefit through unblemished activity, and cultivates the pure ground by practicing the paramita of generosity.

The expanse of the limits of self-nature is vast; the three fundamental afflictions of desire, hatred, and delusion are the conduct [to be purified]. The limit of the vehicle that carries one to the pure state is the authentic practice of sentient beings who are like those afflicted by illness.

The conduct free from defilement is the cause for [rebirth among] devas and humans; in this regard, the excellence of true generosity is such that it nurtures with the affectionate love of a compassionate mother. In various places, the power of repentance is effective; one truly and perfectly bears the burden of virtuous deeds. Following the fragrant substances of tranquility, one seeks the ultimate through the excellence of physical form; yet, there remains a mode of practice that is free from inverted defilements.
Defilements are inexhaustible as one pursues mastery; taking selflessness as the fundamental, the characteristics of birth are all exhausted. In tranquil listening, pride and the like do not arise.

When the root undergoes transformation, that nature of affliction becomes inverted, dark, and dull; though one practices giving, internal strife arises, creating defilement and following after calamity.

The true nature of form is the bondage of craving; knowing the reality of strife and afflictions, one practices the inverted defilement of sovereign bondage; seeking the burden of non-inverted taints, one realizes the truth.

In the pure abode, afflictions are stilled; in the pursuit of transformative practices, the torrential stream arises. Within the celestial realms, purposeful benefit is supreme; through the Bodhisattva’s instructions, one hears and is carried across.

This great king, having been born, practiced giving and performed his duties without error; yet he was bound by the fetters of great craving and would not relinquish them. Lacking the power to restrain himself, he remained distant from pure conduct, thus acting to seek out existence and non-existence, initiating such practices.

Free from defilement, one truly honors that practice; by fundamentally cultivating the veneration of the Tathāgata and seeking its cause, at that time one is naturally free from dullness and ignorance, and follows the silent joy of practicing generosity.

The Buddha-ground is the foremost purity and reality; when conduct accords with virtue and all defilements and obstructions are exhausted, one repents of fundamental karma so that it no longer increases, and sentient beings cultivate the coolness of pure karma.

In this state, the sovereign is pure, wondrous, and supreme; his governance is unerring, rooted in reality, and dedicated to cultivating the highest path toward cessation. When afflictions are exhausted, such giving is performed; seeking the end of perversity, he accords with the cessation of greed. As the fundamental causes of action cease by their very nature, the strife of defilement and the calamities of worldly gain are fully stilled. With the cessation of perverse defilements, the view of self does not arise.

The supreme giving is the unified secret; it is the practice of the fundamental reality of each and every thing. It creates the bonds of defilement and the hindrances that are its root, yet it teaches the cessation of these, leading to tranquility and coolness.

The mind of happiness has purity as its foundation; when afflictions are eliminated at their boundaries, suffering becomes inexhaustible. In this state, the Bodhisattva creates obscurity and arrogance, realizing that understanding the limits of the causes of defilement is of no benefit.

Practicing giving with pure excellence, one is free from the karma of the three miserable realms; following correct principle, one proceeds toward reality. Since there is no end to the manifestations of defiled and evil minds, the king understands therein the methods of governance and transformation; such fundamental discourse is thus characterized by signlessness.

The mental ground truly seeks cessation; through the transformation of the view of self, one aspires for the time when awakened wisdom may come to rest. The bodhisattva’s correct principle is inexhaustible wisdom, wherein the various natures cultivate and honor reality.

Such benefit and purpose are derived from receiving the sacred teachings; in this state of equality, one realizes the truth, wherein the fundamental ground of the mental faculty is supremely pure, and all conditioned transformations and fetters are abandoned.

He brings to rest the afflictions of inversion, fundamental calamities, and defilements; through the increasing power of his meditative coverings, he practices the conduct of cessation. His practice of giving is perfected, his physical marks are complete, and with a pure mind, he undergoes transformation and understands how to act in accordance with reality.

The reflections of one another exist fully within all devas; with pure minds and the like, they are truly without contention. The afflictions of hunger and thirst correspondingly cause destruction, while the dharmas of darkness and pride are unerringly stilled.

The limits of inverted and defiled phenomena are like space; vast compassionate vows are pure and far removed. The nature of bondage is powerful inversion, and the limits of afflictions consist in their respective karmic activities.

Contentious strife blazes like the fire of hatred; when afflictions do not function, ultimate reality possesses power. Its spatial limits are without the characteristics of bondage, and its temporal root destroys the grasping at a self.

The power and function of the quiescent characteristics of sound are perfected; the blazing appearance is the fundamental self-nature; possessing the power of transport, one seeks the vast; and through the causal practice of equanimity, all inversions are exhausted.

The King of Primordial Quiescence possesses a sovereign wisdom and understanding that are difficult to fathom; he thoroughly realizes the true nature of arising from self-nature, is endowed with vast power of knowledge and transformation, and understands arrogance and indulgence through his fearless appearance.

The supreme afflictions are purified and stilled; all excellent tranquility is borne as a burden. This is the pure equality of the noble ones, a secret in which inverted defilements and disputes are entirely exhausted. Thus, the very root of the limits of my bondage—the causes of the taints of affliction—is stilled in profound silence.

The pure physical forms advance in this manner; the movement and cessation are the true nature. Pure appearances are the shifting and changing of physical forms; the Arhats of the four fruits have utterly eliminated the grasping at a self.
That Dharma of silent stillness is excellent practice; by exhausting the root of defilement, this state is pure. The taming of sentient beings relies solely upon skillful instruction.
